question: Is Luxembourg's trade becoming more European, and who changed places outside the EU?
title: Luxembourg's Trade Shift Towards Europe
approach: This chain first measures the share of Luxembourg's trade with the EU versus outside the EU over time to see if it is becoming more European. Then it identifies which non-EU partners changed their trade ranking positions between 2005 and 2025 to understand who changed places outside the EU.

steps.question: What was the share of Luxembourg's total exports by partner group (EU27 vs extra-EU27) in 2005?
steps.purpose: To establish the baseline share of exports to EU and non-EU partners in 2005 for comparison.
steps.queried: exports · EU27 vs non-EU27 · 2005 · share of the whole flow in %
steps.note: In 2005, 80.9% of Luxembourg's exports went to EU27 countries and 19.1% to non-EU27 countries.

steps.question: What was the share of Luxembourg's total exports by partner group (EU27 vs extra-EU27) in 2025?
steps.purpose: To determine the current share of exports to EU and non-EU partners in 2025 for comparison with 2005.
steps.queried: exports · EU27 vs non-EU27 · 2025 · share of the whole flow in %
steps.note: By 2025, exports to EU27 countries rose to 83.1% of total exports, while non-EU27 exports fell to 16.9%.

steps.question: What was the share of Luxembourg's total imports by partner group (EU27 vs extra-EU27) in 2005?
steps.purpose: To establish the baseline share of imports from EU and non-EU partners in 2005 for comparison.
steps.queried: imports · EU27 vs non-EU27 · 2005 · share of the whole flow in %
steps.note: In 2005, 70.3% of Luxembourg's imports came from EU27 countries and 29.7% from non-EU27 countries.

steps.question: What was the share of Luxembourg's total imports by partner group (EU27 vs extra-EU27) in 2025?
steps.purpose: To determine the current share of imports from EU and non-EU partners in 2025 for comparison with 2005.
steps.queried: imports · EU27 vs non-EU27 · 2025 · share of the whole flow in %
steps.note: By 2025, imports from EU27 countries increased to 86.6%, with non-EU27 imports decreasing to 13.4%.

steps.question: Which non-EU partners changed their export ranking positions the most between 2005 and 2025?
steps.purpose: To identify which non-EU partners changed places in Luxembourg's export rankings outside the EU between 2005 and 2025.
steps.queried: exports · non-EU27 partners · by partner (top 10) · 2005–2025 · change between the two years
steps.note: Between 2005 and 2025, Brazil and Canada increased their export values significantly, while the United Kingdom and Russia saw large export declines among non-EU partners.

steps.question: Which non-EU partners changed their import ranking positions the most between 2005 and 2025?
steps.purpose: Step 5 shows which non-EU partners changed their export rankings between 2005 and 2025, but the question also asks about who changed places outside the EU in general, so import ranking changes are needed to complete the picture.
steps.queried: imports · non-EU27 partners · by partner (top 10) · 2005–2025 · change between the two years
steps.note: Japan and Turkey greatly increased their import values and rankings, whereas China and Switzerland experienced large import decreases among non-EU partners.

headline: Luxembourg's trade is becoming more European, with increased shares of both exports and imports within the EU27, while outside the EU, Japan and Turkey rose sharply in import rankings and Brazil and Canada gained in export rankings, whereas the United Kingdom and Russia declined significantly.

points.text: Between 2005 and 2025, Luxembourg's exports to EU27 countries increased their share from 80.9% to 83.1%, while exports to non-EU27 countries decreased from 19.1% to 16.9%, indicating a growing orientation towards European partners in exports.

Imports from EU27 countries rose markedly from 70.3% in 2005 to 86.6% in 2025, while imports from non-EU27 countries fell from 29.7% to 13.4%, showing an even stronger shift towards European sources in imports.

Among non-EU export partners, Brazil and Canada showed the largest increases in export values and ranking positions, with Brazil's exports rising by 184.2% and Canada's by 123.8%, while the United Kingdom and Russia experienced large declines, with UK exports falling by 72.7% and Russian exports by 95.4%.

For non-EU import partners, Japan and Turkey saw the most significant rises in import values and rankings, with Japan's imports increasing by 783.9% and Turkey's by 603.4%, whereas China and Switzerland experienced large decreases, with China's imports falling by 66.1% and Switzerland's by 79.9%.

conclusion: The evidence clearly shows that Luxembourg's trade is becoming more European, with both exports and imports increasingly concentrated within the EU27 between 2005 and 2025. Outside the EU, some partners like Brazil, Canada, Japan, and Turkey have gained prominence in trade rankings, while others such as the United Kingdom, Russia, China, and Switzerland have declined. However, this data does not explain the underlying causes of these shifts or the impact on specific sectors or the economy as a whole.

caveats.message: 1.4 % of this value goes to or comes from undisclosed partners (Q* codes). It stays in the totals but is never ranked or mapped as a country.
Values are in current euros (nominal), not adjusted for price changes.
Intra/extra-EU uses the fixed EU27 (2020) composition; the United Kingdom counts as extra-EU throughout.
